/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 30 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3113 (-65)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4928 (-175)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2384 (-6)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1797 (0)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1012 (-1)
CAPESIZE
All key regions again registered softer rate levels today, resulting in a further $1,584 decline in the BCI 182 5TC to $44,694. Similar weakness was seen in the North Atlantic, where limited support emerged from both trans-Atlantic and fronthaul fixtures. Fixing activity from Brazil/West Africa remained scarce, and with a tender business concluded today for very early November loading, the C3 index fell by just over a dollar to $38.677. In the Pacific, the C5 index extended its decline to $13.445, with two miners reportedly fixing at this level during the day. Despite ongoing pressure on the West Australia/China trade, vessels in the Pacific were increasingly competing for backhaul and Brazil/China cargoes as the ballaster list continued to lengthen.

Atlantic
Eramet was linked to a Koch Newcastlemax for 190,000/10 Owendo to Tianjin 3/9 November at $36.50. An Oldendorff TBN was fixed for 180,000/10 Saldanha Bay to Rotterdam 25 October/3 November at $14.90. Another unnamed vessel from Oldendorff was fixed to TKSE for 180,000/10 Sept-Isles to Rotterdam 20/29 October at $16.70. The Posco tender of 180,000/10 Ubu to Korea 1/5 November was awarded today around $38 C3 equivalent level.

Asia
Rio Tinto took vessels for 170,000/10 Dampier to Qingdao for 16/18 October at $13.40. BHP was linked to the Mount Logan (181,412 2103) and the Global Future (182,613 2025) for 160,000/10 Port Hedland to Qingdao 17/19 October in the $13.40/$13.45 range. Operators paid thick higher with a slightly different loading window.
PANAMAX
The P5TC declined by $49 today to $21,458, with sentiment remaining mixed across both basins. In the Atlantic, trans-Atlantic activity was reported to have slowed when compared to previous sessions. While mineral demand remained evident, particularly from the US East Coast, tonnage supply was generally considered sufficient to meet current requirements. Several market participants also noted that a number of owners were unwilling to entertain prevailing rate levels for trips to the Far East, which helped prevent further downward pressure on sentiment. Elsewhere, EC South America was described as more active, with the October loading window appearing increasingly tight as demand continued to improve. As a result, owners with vessels positioned within this window were reported to be raising their rate expectations, supported by strengthening market fundamentals and a tightening tonnage balance. In the Pacific, sentiment was described as drifting, with Indonesian activity remaining fairly subdued while demand from both Australia and the North Pacific was reported to be relatively steady. Although rates were largely viewed as flat overall, the P3A registered a decline of $169. Owners were generally said to be maintaining their rate expectations despite the softer index performance, while some were also considering ballasting towards EC South America, where improving demand and tightening tonnage fundamentals were seen as offering more attractive employment opportunities.

Atlantic
Sources reported that Bunge had fixed the Ikan Belanak (81,609 2020) open Haldia 22 September for an EC South America fronthaul, with some suggesting the rate to be around $25,000.

Asia
The scrubber-fitted Lowlands Kami (82,459 2024) open Hibikinada 4 October was placed on subjects for an Australia to Singapore-Japan range at $25,100 to Cambrian, while the Bentley (80,856 2019) was reported on subjects from Maoming on 1 October for a similar run. The Guo Yuan 16 (75,915 2012) Kohsichang 1 October was placed on subjects for an Indonesia to Philippines trip with Klaveness, although no other details surfaced.
SUPRAMAX
A rather quiet day with Golden Week looming from tomorrow. Despite the upcoming holiday disruption, rates so far are proving resilient and there is yet to be any sign of levels softening. The Berge Kaizan (63,782 2026) Koh Sichang 7-10 October was said to be on subjects for an Australian round voyage at $23,500, but no further details were available. In the Indian Ocean the Lem Marigold (64,663 2020) Mombasa 6/9 October fixed basis Richards Bay delivery for a trip to Sri Lanka with Oldendorff at $27,000 plus $340,000 ballast bonus and the QC Isabella (63,425 2024) was apparently on subjects basis delivery retroactive Kandla 23 September for a trip via Beira to EC India at $23,000 with Jaldhi. The Atlantic seems to be ticking along without much direction, the Continent having been very firm is now said to be seeing some resistance from Charterers, the Mediterranean remains over supplied and the south Atlantic fairly balanced. After briefly posting gains yesterday, the US Gulf routes returned to negative territory again today, and overall the 11TC average was up just $4 to close at $22,714.
HANDYSIZE
The market experienced a generally slow session, with limited fresh information and little change in underlying dynamics. The BHSI closed at 1,012, while the 7TC average edged down by $16 to finish at $18,210. In the Continent and Mediterranean, fundamentals remained steady despite limited reported activity. The US Gulf was slightly quieter, with reduced cargo enquiry and softer activity contributing to a modest easing in rates. The Yasa Tulip (40,238 2023) was placed on subjects by Pacnav for a grain trip from SW Pass to EC Mexico at $21,500, although further details were not confirmed. The South Atlantic remained balanced, with rates holding steady. A modern 40,000-dwt vessel was heard fixed for a trip from Recalada to the Far East in the mid-$20,000s, although further details were lacking. Views in the Pacific were mixed with some sources reporting a modest pickup in activity and firmer rates as tonnage tightened, while others described the market as finely balanced or slightly softer.

Market Fundamentals
Brazil’s CSN Pauses Low-Grade Iron Ore Production

Brazil’s CSN Mineracao announced a reduction to low-grade iron ore output at its Pires Complex dry processing plant, citing elevated Brazil-China freight costs alongside challenging market conditions, according to a filing with the US SEC. The company lowered its 2026 guidance for production and third-party purchase volumes by 6 Mt to 39-41 Mt, while unit cost guidance was raised from $22.00-23.50/t to $25.00-26.00/t. In its latest investor report, the company’s total iron ore production in stood 0.8 Mt below the prior year at 21.0 Mt in 1h26.
